# Compiling data tables and managing duplicates

## Pink seedlings

Importing DATA

```{r}
previous_data = read.csv("Raw_data/ARTEMIA_suivi_plantules_ALLDATA_03-2026.csv", header =T, sep=",",dec=".") # data import
str(previous_data) # checking the type of variables - all is OK 

browsing_pink = read.csv("Raw_data/Feuille terrain FTH 2026 Abrout. ROSE.csv", header =T, sep=";",dec=",")
str(browsing_pink) # all the variable are well defined

growth_pink = read.csv("Raw_data/Copie de Feuille terrain FTH 2026 Ecophy ROSE.csv", header =T, sep=",",dec=".") # "," changed to "."
str(growth_pink)  # all the "numeric" variables are defined as "character"
growth_pink = growth_pink %>% mutate_at(c(4:14),as.numeric) # transform the columns from 4 to 14 into numerical 

light = read.csv("Raw_data/Donnees_Lumiere_associees.csv", header =T, sep=";",dec=".") 
str(light) # two columns are misidentified

```

Modifications of different data tables for "pink" seedlings

```{r}
# Modification of "browsing" table 
browsing_pink = browsing_pink[,c(2,3,10,11,12)]
browsing_pink = browsing_pink %>% rename(Etat_09.26=Etat, Abrout_09.26=Abrout.,Commentaire_09.26 = Commentaire,Bague=Bague_R)
browsing_pink = browsing_pink %>% rename(Commentaire_Abrout_09.26 = Commentaire_09.26)
browsing_pink$Type_bis = ifelse(startsWith(browsing_pink$Placette,"TC"), "CONTROL","TRANSECT") 
browsing_pink= browsing_pink[,-1]

# Modification of "growth" table
growth_pink = growth_pink[,-c(1)]
colnames(growth_pink) <- paste(colnames(growth_pink), "09.26", sep = "_") # adding a suffix to all columns
growth_pink = growth_pink %>% rename(Bague = Bague_R_09.26) 
growth_pink = growth_pink %>% rename(Placette = Placette_09.26) 
growth_pink = growth_pink %>% rename(Commentaire_Ecophy_09.26 = Comm_09.26)
growth_pink$Type_bis = ifelse(startsWith(growth_pink$Placette,"TC"), "CONTROL","TRANSECT") 
growth_pink= growth_pink[,-1]

# Modification of "light" table 
colnames(light) <- paste(colnames(light), "09.26", sep = "_")
light = light %>% rename(Bague = Bague_09.26) 
light = light %>% rename(Commentaire_light_09.26 = Commentaire_09.26)
light$Type_bis = ifelse(light$Type == "CONTROL", "CONTROL","TRANSECT")
light_pink = subset(light, light$Bague < 2000) # 1944 seedlings were subsetted in a new table. (Within light measurements every plant ring above 2000 belongs to new seedlings therefore excluded here). 
light_pink_TC = subset(light_pink, light_pink$Type_bis == "TRANSECT") 
light_pink_C = subset(light_pink, light_pink$Type_bis == "CONTROL")

light_pink_duplicates_TC = light_pink_TC %>% group_by(Bague) %>% mutate(nbdoublons=n()) # number of duplicates are searched
sum(light_pink_duplicates_TC$nbdoublons>1) # no duplicates

light_pink_duplicates_C = light_pink_C %>% group_by(Bague) %>% mutate(nbdoublons=n()) # number of duplicates are searched
sum(light_pink_duplicates_C$nbdoublons >1) # no duplicates
light = light[, -c(1:3,5)]

# Modification of "previous_data" table
previous_data$Type_bis = ifelse(previous_data$Type=="CONTROL", "CONTROL","TRANSECT")

```

Combining datasets for data alignment

```{r}
pink_data = left_join(previous_data, browsing_pink, by=(c("Bague" = "Bague", "Type_bis" = "Type_bis")))
pink_data = left_join(pink_data, growth_pink)
pink_data = left_join(pink_data, light) # Each row now represents a seedling with all of its corresponding data variables :) 
pink_data_clean = pink_data[,-c(1,68)]
sum(is.na(pink_data_clean$ER_09.26))
```

Now we check the problem of two columns of "state alive and death

```{r}
# First change the "/" and "-" into NA
pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y[pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y == "-" | pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y == "/"] <- NA

pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.x[pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.x == "-" | pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.x == "/"] <- NA

# Complete the columns Etat_09.26.x with the information of Etat_09.26.y

pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y <- ifelse(is.na(pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y) & 
                                 (pink_data_clean$Haut_cm_09.26 == 0 | pink_data_clean$Haut_cm_09.26 == "" |
                                    is.na(pink_data_clean$Haut_cm_09.26) | pink_data_clean$D1_mm_09.26 == 0 | is.na(pink_data_clean$D1_mm_09.26) |
                                    pink_data_clean$D1_mm_09.26 == ""
                                  | pink_data_clean$D2_mm_09.26 == 0 | is.na(pink_data_clean$D2_mm_09.26) | pink_data_clean$D2_mm_09.26 != "" ),
                                 pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.x, pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y)

# Complete the columns Etat_09.26.x with the information of Etat_03.26
pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y  = ifelse(pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y ==""&pink_data_clean$Etat_03.26=="M", pink_data_clean$Etat_03.26,pink_data_clean$Etat_09.26.y )
  
# Delete the useless columns 
pink_data_clean = pink_data_clean[,-66]
```

Now we create a data frame with the seedlings having NA for the mesure of 09/2026 and the data.frame for the death/alive seedlings

```{r}
Missing_value_pink = pink_data_clean[!complete.cases(pink_data_clean[, -c(1:65,75:79)]),] # this is all the lines with missing value except for herbivory

# We subset only for the alive seedlings
Missing_value_pink_alive = subset(Missing_value_pink, Missing_value_pink$Etat_09.26.y=="V")
write.csv(Missing_value_pink_alive, "Missing_value_pink.csv") # we have 75 seedlings alive with missing value (probably mainly light)
sum(is.na(Missing_value_pink_alive$ER_09.26)) # we have 30 data light missing


# Dead alive seedlings 
Undead_pink <- pink_data_clean %>% mutate(Undead = ifelse(Etat_09.26.y == "M", ifelse(Haut_cm_09.26 != 0 & !is.na(Haut_cm_09.26) & Haut_cm_09.26!= "" & D1_mm_09.26 != 0 & !is.na(D1_mm_09.26) & D1_mm_09.26 != "" & D2_mm_09.26 != 0 & !is.na(D2_mm_09.26) & D2_mm_09.26 != "", T, F), F)) %>% filter(Undead == T)

write_csv(Undead_pink,"undead_pink.csv")

# Alive dead seedlings
not_alive_pink <- pink_data_clean %>% mutate(not_alive = ifelse(Etat_09.26.y == "V", ifelse((Haut_cm_09.26 == 0 | is.na(Haut_cm_09.26) | Haut_cm_09.26 == "")&(D1_mm_09.26 == 0 | is.na(D1_mm_09.26) | D1_mm_09.26 == "" )&(
  D2_mm_09.26 == 0 | is.na(D2_mm_09.26) | D2_mm_09.26 == ""), T, F), F)) %>% filter(not_alive == T)

write_csv(not_alive_pink,"not_alive_pink.csv")

```

Rename columns for association of data set

```{r}
pink_data_clean = pink_data_clean %>% rename(Etat_09.26 = Etat_09.26.y)
```

herbivory (insect) detection of inconsistencies

(modified directly on the data)

```{r}
#On cherche les colones qui ont des incoherences d'herbivory
df_checked_pink <- pink_data_clean %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    # Compter les colonnes Herb_1:Herb_5 qui sont ni NA ni 0
    n_herb_cols = sum(!is.na(c_across(Herb1_09.26:Herb5_09.26)) & c_across(Herb1_09.26:Herb5_09.26) != 0),
    
    # Valeur attendue (N_herb plafonné à 5)
    attendu = ifelse(Nherb_09.26 > 5, 5, Nherb_09.26),
    
    # Test de cohérence
    erreur = n_herb_cols != attendu
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Filtrer uniquement les incohérences
df_checked_pink <- df_checked_pink %>% filter(erreur)

```

Creation of a predicted diameter

```{r}

# Détection des valeurs de diamètre trop différentes
err_diam_pink <- pink_data_clean %>%
  mutate(
    diff_pct_Diam = abs(D2_mm_09.26 - D1_mm_09.26) /
      ((D1_mm_09.26 + D2_mm_09.26) / 2) * 100,
    diff_Diam = abs(D1_mm_09.26 - D2_mm_09.26)
  ) %>%
  filter(diff_pct_Diam >= 20 & diff_Diam >= 0.5)


# Régression linéaire
df_filtered_rose <- pink_data_clean %>%
  mutate(
    D_moy_09.26 = (D1_mm_09.26 + D2_mm_09.26) / 2,
    diff_pct_Diam = abs(D2_mm_09.26 - D1_mm_09.26) /
      D_moy_09.26 * 100,
    diff_Diam = abs(D1_mm_09.26 - D2_mm_09.26)
  ) %>%
  filter(diff_pct_Diam <= 20 & diff_Diam <= 0.5)

# Ajustement du modèle de prédiction
m_quad_rose <- lm(
  D_moy_09.26 ~ Haut_cm_09.26 + I(Haut_cm_09.26^2),
  data = df_filtered_rose
)

# Application du modèle : ajout du diamètre moyen et de la prédiction
pink_data_clean <- pink_data_clean %>%
  mutate(
    D_moy_09.26 = (D1_mm_09.26 + D2_mm_09.26) / 2,
    Pred_D_moy_09.26 = predict(m_quad_rose, newdata = pink_data_clean)
  )

# Ajout des prédictions dans le tableau des diamètres incohérents
err_diam_pink <- err_diam_pink %>%
  left_join(
    pink_data_clean %>%
      select(Bague, Transect, D1_mm_09.26, D2_mm_09.26,
             Pred_D_moy_09.26),
    by = c("Bague", "Transect", "D1_mm_09.26", "D2_mm_09.26"),
    suffix = c("", "_pred")
  )

# Remplacement du diamètre moyen par le diamètre le plus proche
# de la prédiction
err_diam_pink <- err_diam_pink %>%
  mutate(
    D_closest = ifelse(
      abs(D1_mm_09.26 - Pred_D_moy_09.26) <=
        abs(D2_mm_09.26 - Pred_D_moy_09.26),
      D1_mm_09.26,
      D2_mm_09.26
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(D_moy_09.26 = D_closest) %>%
  select(-D_closest, -diff_pct_Diam, -diff_Diam)

# On ajoute les lignes corrigées au tableau original
pink_data_clean <- pink_data_clean %>%
  anti_join(
    err_diam_pink,
    by = c("Bague", "Transect", "D1_mm_09.26", "D2_mm_09.26")
  ) %>%
  bind_rows(err_diam_pink)


```

The data are in "raw_data_modified" file because the empty lines were delete directly in Excel.


Modification of "orange" data tables

```{r}
## Modifications of "Browsing" data
Browsing_Orange = Browsing_Orange[, c(3,4,5,6,7)] #removing unnecessary columns
#renaming columns
colnames(Browsing_Orange) <- paste(colnames(Browsing_Orange), "09.26", sep = "_") 
Browsing_Orange = Browsing_Orange %>% rename(Bague = Bague_O_09.26)
Browsing_Orange = Browsing_Orange %>% rename(Commentaire_Abrout_09.26 = Commentaire_09.26)
Browsing_Orange$Type_bis = ifelse(startsWith(Browsing_Orange$Placette, "TC"), "CONTROL", "TRANSECT") #Creation of a new column that clearly separates "control" and "transect" seedlings
Browsing_Orange = Browsing_Orange[, -1] #removal of the column "Placette"

## Modifications of "Growth" data
Growth_Orange = Growth_Orange[,-1:-2]
# We rename colones
colnames(Growth_Orange) <- paste(colnames(Growth_Orange), "09.26", sep = "_")
Growth_Orange = Growth_Orange %>% rename(Bague = Bague_O_09.26)
Growth_Orange = Growth_Orange %>% rename(Commentaire_Ecophy_09.26 = Comm_09.26)
Growth_Orange$Type_bis = ifelse(startsWith(Growth_Orange$Carre, "TC"), "CONTROL", "TRANSECT") #Creation of a new column that clearly separates "control" and "transect" seedlings
Growth_Orange = Growth_Orange[, -1] #removal of the column "Placette"

## Modifications of "Genetic" data 
Genet_Orange$Type_bis = ifelse(startsWith(Genet_Orange$T, "TC"), "CONTROL", "TRANSECT")
# Changing the format of the values in the "Placette" and "Piquet_ref" columns
Genet_Orange <- Genet_Orange %>% mutate(Piquet_Ref = ifelse(str_starts(Piquet_Ref, "T"), Piquet_Ref, ifelse(str_starts(Piquet_Ref,"C[A-Za-z]"), paste("T",Piquet_Ref, sep = ""), paste(T,Piquet_Ref, sep = "")))) %>% mutate(Placette = ifelse(str_starts(Placette, "T"), Placette, ifelse(str_starts(Placette, "C[A-Za-z]"), paste("T", Placette, sep = ""), paste(T, Placette, sep = ""))))
#Creation of a new column that clearly separates "control" and "transect" seedlings
Genet_Orange = Genet_Orange %>% rename(Bague = Bague_O) #renaming a column
Genet_Orange = Genet_Orange %>% rename(Commentaire_Genet_09.26 = Comm)

## Data compilation and alignment
Data_Orange_1 <- left_join(Genet_Orange, Browsing_Orange)
Data_Orange_2 <- left_join(Data_Orange_1, Growth_Orange)
```

## Mapping of seedlings

We extract the locations for the orange and pink seedlings.

```{r}
Local_Seedling <- Merged_Pink_Orange %>% select(c(Bague, Placette, Piquet_ref, Azimut, Dist_m))
```

We read the layer with the stake locations

```{r}
Geom_Stake <- st_read("Mapping/Previous_layers/Piquets_tous.gpkg")
```

We project the localisation of the seedlings thanks to the localisation of the stakes

```{r}
# We join the two dataframe to associate at the orange seedlings the localisation of their reference stake
Local_Seedling <- left_join(Local_Seedling, as.data.frame(Geom_Stake) %>% rename(Piquet_ref = name), join_by (Piquet_ref))
# We calculate the localisations of the seedlings thanks to trigonometric formula
Local_Seedling <- Local_Seedling %>% mutate(angle = Azimut*pi/180) %>% mutate(X_plantule = Coord_X + sin(angle) * Dist_m) %>% mutate(Y_plantule = Coord_Y + cos(angle) * Dist_m) %>% mutate(Coord_X = X_plantule, Coord_Y = Y_plantule) %>% mutate(Coord_X = X_plantule, Coord_Y = Y_plantule) %>% filter(!is.na(X_plantule), !is.na(Y_plantule)) %>% select(c(- X_plantule, - Y_plantule, - angle))
```

We create the layers of seedlings localisations

```{r}
# We create the layers
Geom_Seedling <- st_as_sf(Local_Seedling, coords = c("Coord_X","Coord_Y")) %>% select(-geom)

# We choose their Coordinate Reference Systems (CRS)
Geom_Seedling <- st_set_crs(Geom_Seedling, 2972)
```

We can export the layers

```{r}

#st_write(Geom_Seedling %>% filter(Bague < 2000), "Mapping/Exported_layers/Pink_seeldlings.shp")
```

## Mapping of sensors

It's the same method as for seedlings

```{r}
Local_Sensor <- read.csv("Mapping/Capteurs_ARTEMIA.csv", sep = ";", dec =",")

# We change the format of the values in the "Piquet_ref" column
Local_Sensor <- Local_Sensor %>% mutate(Piquet_ref = paste(Transect, Piquet_ref, sep = ""))

# We calculate the coordinates
Local_Sensor <- Local_Sensor %>% left_join(as.data.frame(Geom_Stake) %>% rename(Piquet_ref = name)) %>% mutate(angle = Azimut*pi/180) %>% mutate(X_sensor = Coord_X + sin(angle) * Dist) %>% mutate(Y_sensor = Coord_Y + cos(angle) * Dist) %>% mutate(Coord_X = X_sensor, Coord_Y = Y_sensor) %>% filter(!is.na(X_sensor), !is.na(Y_sensor)) %>% select(c(-X_sensor, -Y_sensor, -angle))

# We filter the two types of sensor and we creat their layer
Geom_Sensor <- st_as_sf(Local_Sensor, coords = c("Coord_X", "Coord_Y")) %>% st_set_crs(2972)
```

We can export the layers

```{r}
#st_write(Geom_Sensor %>% filter(Capteur == "TMS4"), "Mapping/Exported_layers/TMS4.shp")
#st_write(Geom_Sensor %>% filter(Capteur == "EL-USB-2"), "Mapping/Exported_layers/EL_USB_2.shp")
```

## Distance between seedlings and skid trails

Read the skid trails layer

```{r}
Geom_Skid_Trail <- st_read("Mapping/previous_layers/pistes_debardage.gpkg")
```

calculate distances

```{r}
# We only keep the seedlings located in the transects, excluding those in the control plot, since it contains no skid trails
Geom_Seedling_Transect <- Geom_Seedling %>% filter(Transect != "TC")

# Both layers are in EPSG:2972, so we can compute seedling-to-skid-trail minimum distances
Geom_Seedling_Transect <- Geom_Seedling_Transect %>% mutate(Dist_skid_trails = as.numeric(st_distance(Geom_Seedling_Transect, st_union(Geom_Skid_Trail))))
```

We add this variable to our data frame : Merged_Pink_Orange

```{r}
Merged_Pink_Orange <- left_join(Merged_Pink_Orange, st_drop_geometry(Geom_Seedling_Transect))
```

## Distance and ID of the nearest TMS4 sensor and the nearest EL-USB-2 sensor for each seedling

```{r}
# Both layers use EPSG:2972, so we can compute the minimum distances from each seedling to the nearest TMS4 and EL-USB-2 sensors
Geom_Seedling <- Geom_Seedling %>% mutate(Dist_TMS4 = as.numeric(st_distance(Geom_Seedling, st_union(Geom_Sensor %>% filter(Capteur == 'TMS4'))))) %>% mutate(Dist_EL_USB_2 = as.numeric(st_distance(Geom_Seedling, st_union(Geom_Sensor %>% filter(Capteur == 'EL-USB-2')))))

# We add the ID of the nearest sensor TMS4 and the nearest sensor EL-USB-2
Geom_TMS4 <- Geom_Sensor %>% filter(Capteur == "TMS4")
Geom_EL_USB_2 <- Geom_Sensor %>% filter(Capteur == "EL-USB-2")

Geom_Seedling <- Geom_Seedling %>% mutate(ID_TMS4 = Geom_TMS4$Code_capteur[st_nearest_feature(., Geom_TMS4)]) %>% mutate(ID_EL_USB_2 = Geom_EL_USB_2$Code_capteur[st_nearest_feature(., Geom_EL_USB_2)])
```

We add these variables to our data frame : Merged_Pink_Orange

```{r}
Merged_Pink_Orange <- Merged_Pink_Orange %>% left_join(., st_drop_geometry(Geom_Seedling))
```

```{r}
write.csv(Merged_Pink_Orange, "Exported_data/ARTEMIA_seedling_monitoring_ALLDATA_09_2026.csv")
```

## Importing Data

Data

```{r}
TOMST <- read.csv("Captor_data/Alldata_TOMST.csv", header = T, sep = ";", dec = ",")
LASCARS <- read.csv("Captor_data/Alldata_LASCARS.csv", header = T, sep = ",", dec = ".")
Seedling <- Merged_Pink_Orange
```

Geometry Layers

```{r}
geom_lascar <- st_read("Mapping/Exported_layers/EL_USB_2.shp")
geom_tomst <- st_read("Mapping/Exported_layers/TMS4.shp")
geom_stake <- st_read("Mapping/Previous_layers/Piquets_tous.gpkg")
id_plot <- read.csv("Raw_data/polygone_plot.csv", sep = ",")
```

Compute the center of each plot

```{r}
# long format for id_plot
plot <- id_plot %>% pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Stake"), names_to = "order", values_to = "id_stake")

# join the geometry with the plot
plot_stake <- left_join(plot, geom_stake, by = c("id_stake" = "name")) %>% st_as_sf()

# creation of the polygons
geom_plot <- plot_stake %>% arrange(Plot, order) %>% group_by(Plot) %>% summarise(do_union = FALSE) %>% st_cast("POLYGON") # create closed polygons

plot(geom_plot)

geom_plot <- st_set_crs(geom_plot, 2972)

geom_plot_no_chablis <- geom_plot %>% filter(!(Plot %in% c("TCB3_chablis", "TCC3_chablis", "TCC4_chablis", "TCD4_chablis"))) 

# st_write(geom_plot, "Layers/plot.gpkg")

geom_center_plot <- st_centroid(geom_plot)

plot(geom_center_plot)

# st_write(geom_center_plot, "Layers/center_plot.gpkg")
```

## Data preparation

### Canopy openess (Fisheye pictures)

```{r}
CO <- Seedling %>% dplyr::select(Transect, Placette, CO_mean_09.25) %>% filter(!is.na(CO_mean_09.25)) %>% group_by(Placette) %>% summarise(Transect = first(Transect),CO_mean_09.25 = mean(CO_mean_09.25)) %>% ungroup()

CO <- CO %>% mutate(Placette = ifelse(Placette == "T4A0 ", "T4A0", Placette))
CO <- CO %>% mutate(Placette = ifelse(Placette == "TAB1", "T4B1", Placette))
CO <- CO %>% group_by(Placette) %>% summarise(CO_mean_09.25 = mean(CO_mean_09.25))

CO <- CO %>% mutate(Placette = ifelse(
  Placette == "TCB3", "TCB3_chablis", ifelse(
    Placette == "TCC3", "TCC3_chablis", ifelse(
      Placette == "TCC4", "TCC4_chablis", ifelse(
        Placette == "TCD4", "TCD4_chablis", Placette))))
)
```

We have one value of Canopy Openess (CO) for each plot.

### TOMST

```{r}
# We add the column Transect
TOMST <- TOMST %>% mutate(serial_number = as.character(serial_number)) %>% mutate(Transect = ifelse(endsWith(serial_number, "31")|endsWith(serial_number, "32")|endsWith(serial_number, "33")|endsWith(serial_number, "34")|endsWith(serial_number, "35"), "T1", ifelse(endsWith(serial_number, "36")|endsWith(serial_number, "37")|endsWith(serial_number, "48")|endsWith(serial_number, "49")|endsWith(serial_number, "50"), "T2", ifelse(endsWith(serial_number, "51")|endsWith(serial_number, "52")|endsWith(serial_number, "53")|endsWith(serial_number, "54")|endsWith(serial_number, "55"), "T3", ifelse(endsWith(serial_number, "56")|endsWith(serial_number, "57")|endsWith(serial_number, "58")|endsWith(serial_number, "59")|endsWith(serial_number, "60"), "T4", ifelse(endsWith(serial_number, "61")|endsWith(serial_number, "62")|endsWith(serial_number, "63")|endsWith(serial_number, "64")|endsWith(serial_number, "65"), "T5", ifelse(endsWith(serial_number, "66")|endsWith(serial_number, "67")|endsWith(serial_number, "68")|endsWith(serial_number, "69")|endsWith(serial_number, "70"), "T6", ifelse(endsWith(serial_number, "71")|endsWith(serial_number, "72")|endsWith(serial_number, "73")|endsWith(serial_number, "74")|endsWith(serial_number, "75"), "TC", "TC_chablis"))))))))

# We separate the date and the time
TOMST <- TOMST %>% separate(datetime_UTC, c("Date", "Time"), sep = " ") %>% mutate(Time = ifelse(is.na(Time), "0:00", Time)) %>% separate(Time, c("Hour", "Minutes"), convert = TRUE, remove = FALSE) %>% mutate(serial_number = as.character(serial_number))
```

we compute the max value for each day and each sensors

```{r}
max_tomst <- TOMST %>% group_by(serial_number, Date, height) %>% summarise(
  max_value = max(value),
  min_value = min(value)
)

max_tomst_Tair <- max_tomst %>% filter(height == "air 14 cm") %>% 
  rename("max_T_air_tomst" = "max_value", "min_T_air_tomst" = "min_value") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-height)

max_tomst_Tsoil16 <- max_tomst %>% filter(height == "soil 16 cm") %>% 
  rename("max_T_soil_16cm" = "max_value", "min_T_soil_16cm" = "min_value") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-height)

max_tomst_Tsoil26 <- max_tomst %>% filter(height == "soil 26 cm") %>% 
  rename("max_T_soil_26cm" = "max_value", "min_T_soil_26cm" = "min_value") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-height)

max_tomst_Hsoil <- max_tomst %>% filter(height == "soil 18-33 cm") %>% 
  rename("max_H_soil" = "max_value", "min_H_soil" = "min_value") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-height)

max_tomst <- left_join(max_tomst_Tsoil16, max_tomst_Tsoil26)
max_tomst <- left_join(max_tomst, max_tomst_Hsoil)
max_tomst <- left_join(max_tomst, max_tomst_Tair)

mean_max_tomst <- max_tomst %>% group_by(serial_number) %>% summarise(
  mean_max_T_air_tomst = mean(max_T_air_tomst),
  mean_min_T_air_tomst = mean(min_T_air_tomst),
  mean_max_T_soil_16cm = mean(max_T_soil_16cm),
  mean_min_T_soil_16cm = mean(min_T_soil_16cm),
  mean_max_T_soil_26cm = mean(max_T_soil_26cm),
  mean_min_T_soil_26cm = mean(min_T_soil_26cm),
  mean_max_H_soil = mean(max_H_soil),
  mean_min_H_soil = mean(min_H_soil)
)
```

### LASCAR

```{r}
# We fix the name of LASCAR sensor
LASCARS <- LASCARS %>% mutate(id_capteur = ifelse(id_capteur == '"T5_2_20"', "T5_2_20", id_capteur))

# We separate the date and the time
LASCARS <- LASCARS %>% separate(time, c("Date", "Time"), sep = " ") %>% mutate(Time = ifelse(is.na(Time), "0:00", Time)) %>% separate(Time, c("Hour", "Minutes"), convert = TRUE, remove = FALSE)
```

we compute the max value for each day and each sensors

```{r}
max_lascar <- LASCARS %>% group_by(id_capteur, Date) %>% summarise(
  max_T_air = max(celsius_c), 
  max_H_air = max(humidity_percent_rh), 
  min_T_air = min(celsius_c), 
  min_H_air = min(humidity_percent_rh)
)

mean_max_lascar <- max_lascar %>% group_by(id_capteur) %>% summarise(
  mean_max_T_air = mean(max_T_air), 
  mean_min_T_air = mean(min_T_air), 
  mean_max_H_air = mean(max_H_air), 
  mean_min_H_air = mean(min_H_air)
)
```

We give to each plot his data

First we find the intersection between our plot and our sensors to see which sensor are in which plot

```{r}
inter_lascar_plot <- st_intersection(geom_lascar, geom_plot)
inter_tomst_plot <- st_intersection(geom_tomst, geom_plot)
# st_write(inter_lascar_plot, "Layers/inter_lascar_plot.gpkg")
# st_write(inter_tomst_plot, "Layers/inter_tomst_plot.gpkg")
```

Then, we compute the distance between each plot center and his closest sensor.

TOMST

```{r}
geom_tomst_without_na <- geom_tomst %>% mutate(Cmplmnt = ifelse(is.na(Cmplmnt), "not chablis", Cmplmnt))

geom_tomst_no_chablis <- geom_tomst_without_na %>% filter(Cmplmnt != "Chablis")

geom_tomst_chablis <- geom_tomst_without_na %>% filter(Cmplmnt == "Chablis")

geom_plot_tomst_no_chablis <- geom_plot_no_chablis %>% mutate(dist_tomst = as.numeric(st_distance(geom_center_plot %>% filter(!(Plot %in% c("TCB3_chablis", "TCC3_chablis", "TCC4_chablis", "TCD4_chablis"))), st_union(geom_tomst_no_chablis)))) %>% mutate(id_tomst = geom_tomst_no_chablis$Cd_cptr[st_nearest_feature(.,geom_tomst_no_chablis)])

geom_plot_tomst_chablis <- geom_plot %>% filter(Plot %in% c("TCB3_chablis", "TCC3_chablis", "TCC4_chablis", "TCD4_chablis")) %>% 
  mutate(dist_tomst = as.numeric(st_distance(geom_center_plot %>% filter(Plot %in% c("TCB3_chablis", "TCC3_chablis", "TCC4_chablis", "TCD4_chablis")), st_union(geom_tomst_chablis)))) %>% mutate(id_tomst = geom_tomst_chablis$Cd_cptr[st_nearest_feature(.,geom_tomst_chablis)])
```

LASCAR

```{r}
# We calculate the distance between the plot and the lascar without chablis on the TC
geom_lascar_without_na <- geom_lascar %>% mutate(Cmplmnt = ifelse(is.na(Cmplmnt), "not chablis", Cmplmnt))

geom_lascar_no_chablis <- geom_lascar_without_na %>% filter(Cmplmnt != "Chablis")

geom_lascar_chablis <- geom_lascar_without_na %>% filter(Cmplmnt == "Chablis")


geom_plot_no_chablis <- geom_plot %>% filter(!(Plot %in% c("TCB3_chablis", "TCC3_chablis", "TCC4_chablis", "TCD4_chablis"))) 

geom_plot_lascar_no_chablis <- geom_plot_no_chablis %>% mutate(dist_lascar = as.numeric(st_distance(geom_center_plot %>% filter(!(Plot %in% c("TCB3_chablis", "TCC3_chablis", "TCC4_chablis", "TCD4_chablis"))), st_union(geom_lascar_no_chablis)))) %>% mutate(id_lascar = geom_lascar_no_chablis$Cd_cptr[st_nearest_feature(.,geom_lascar_no_chablis)])

#Now, for the chablis
geom_plot_lascar_chablis <- geom_plot %>% filter(Plot %in% c("TCB3_chablis", "TCC3_chablis", "TCC4_chablis", "TCD4_chablis")) %>% 
  mutate(dist_lascar = as.numeric(st_distance(geom_center_plot %>% filter(Plot %in% c("TCB3_chablis", "TCC3_chablis", "TCC4_chablis", "TCD4_chablis")), st_union(geom_lascar_chablis)))) %>% mutate(id_lascar = geom_lascar_chablis$Cd_cptr[st_nearest_feature(.,geom_lascar_chablis)])
```

We can fusion the data

```{r}
fus_lascar <- bind_rows(geom_plot_lascar_no_chablis, geom_plot_lascar_chablis)
fus_tomst <- bind_rows(geom_plot_tomst_no_chablis, geom_plot_tomst_chablis)
fus_lascar <- st_drop_geometry(fus_lascar)
fus_tomst <- st_drop_geometry(fus_tomst)

plot_sensor_dist <- left_join(fus_tomst, fus_lascar)
```

We compute for each plot the mean of their sensors which intersect this plot

TOMST

```{r}
inter_tomst_plot <- inter_tomst_plot %>% mutate(Cd_cptr = paste("966815", Cd_cptr, sep = ''))

data_tomst_inter <- left_join(mean_max_tomst, inter_tomst_plot, join_by(serial_number == Cd_cptr)) %>% filter(!is.na(Plot))

data_tomst_inter <- data_tomst_inter %>% dplyr::select(serial_number, mean_max_T_air_tomst, mean_min_T_air_tomst, mean_max_T_soil_16cm, mean_min_T_soil_16cm, mean_max_T_soil_26cm, mean_min_T_soil_26cm, mean_max_H_soil, mean_min_H_soil, Plot) %>% group_by(Plot) %>% summarise(
  mean_max_T_air_tomst = mean(mean_max_T_air_tomst),
  mean_min_T_air_tomst = mean(mean_min_T_air_tomst),
  mean_max_T_soil_16cm = mean(mean_max_T_soil_16cm), 
  mean_min_T_soil_16cm = mean(mean_min_T_soil_16cm), 
  mean_max_T_soil_26cm = mean(mean_max_T_soil_26cm), 
  mean_min_T_soil_26cm = mean(mean_min_T_soil_26cm),
  mean_max_H_soil = mean(mean_max_H_soil), 
  mean_min_H_soil = mean(mean_min_H_soil)
)
```

LASCAR

```{r}
inter_lascar_plot <- inter_lascar_plot %>% mutate(Cd_cptr = gsub("-", "_", Cd_cptr))

data_lascar_inter <- left_join(mean_max_lascar, inter_lascar_plot, join_by(id_capteur == Cd_cptr)) %>% filter(!is.na(Plot))

data_lascar_inter <- data_lascar_inter %>% dplyr::select(id_capteur, mean_max_T_air, mean_min_T_air, mean_max_H_air, mean_min_H_air, Plot) %>% group_by(Plot) %>% summarise(
  mean_max_T_air = mean(mean_max_T_air),
  mean_min_T_air = mean(mean_min_T_air),
  mean_max_H_air = mean(mean_max_H_air), 
  mean_min_H_air = mean(mean_min_H_air)
)
```

We give to each intersect plot the value of the sensors which intersect him

```{r}
# data according to distance
plot_sensor_dist <- plot_sensor_dist %>% mutate(
  id_lascar = gsub("-", "_", id_lascar), 
  id_tomst = paste("966815", id_tomst, sep = ""))

data_plot_dist <- left_join(plot_sensor_dist, mean_max_lascar, join_by(id_lascar == id_capteur))

data_plot_dist <- left_join(data_plot_dist, mean_max_tomst, join_by(id_tomst == serial_number))

## LASCAR
# We replace the value with those in the intersection
data_lascar <- data_plot_dist %>% mutate(
  mean_max_T_air = ifelse(Plot %in% data_lascar_inter$Plot, data_lascar_inter$mean_max_T_air[which(data_lascar_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_max_T_air), 
  mean_min_T_air = ifelse(Plot %in% data_lascar_inter$Plot, data_lascar_inter$mean_min_T_air[which(data_lascar_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_min_T_air),
  mean_max_H_air = ifelse(Plot %in% data_lascar_inter$Plot, data_lascar_inter$mean_max_H_air[which(data_lascar_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_max_H_air),
  mean_min_H_air = ifelse(Plot %in% data_lascar_inter$Plot, data_lascar_inter$mean_min_H_air[which(data_lascar_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_min_H_air),
)

## TOMST
data_lascar_tomst <- data_lascar %>% mutate(
  mean_max_T_air_tomst = ifelse(Plot %in% data_tomst_inter$Plot, data_tomst_inter$mean_max_T_air_tomst[which(data_tomst_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_max_T_air_tomst),
  mean_min_T_air_tomst = ifelse(Plot %in% data_tomst_inter$Plot, data_tomst_inter$mean_min_T_air_tomst[which(data_tomst_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_min_T_air_tomst),
  mean_max_T_soil_16cm = ifelse(Plot %in% data_tomst_inter$Plot, data_tomst_inter$mean_max_T_soil_16cm[which(data_tomst_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_max_T_soil_16cm),
  mean_min_T_soil_16cm = ifelse(Plot %in% data_tomst_inter$Plot, data_tomst_inter$mean_min_T_soil_16cm[which(data_tomst_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_min_T_soil_16cm),
  mean_max_T_soil_26cm = ifelse(Plot %in% data_tomst_inter$Plot, data_tomst_inter$mean_max_T_soil_26cm[which(data_tomst_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_max_T_soil_26cm),
  mean_min_T_soil_26cm = ifelse(Plot %in% data_tomst_inter$Plot, data_tomst_inter$mean_min_T_soil_26cm[which(data_tomst_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_min_T_soil_26cm),
  mean_max_H_soil = ifelse(Plot %in% data_tomst_inter$Plot, data_tomst_inter$mean_max_H_soil[which(data_tomst_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_max_H_soil),
  mean_min_H_soil = ifelse(Plot %in% data_tomst_inter$Plot, data_tomst_inter$mean_min_H_soil[which(data_tomst_inter$Plot == Plot)], mean_min_H_soil),
)
```

We fusion the data to do the PCA

```{r}
data <- data_lascar_tomst %>% dplyr::select(-dist_tomst, -dist_lascar, -id_tomst, -id_lascar) 

data <- left_join(data, CO, join_by(Plot == Placette))

data <- data %>% mutate(type = ifelse(
  startsWith(Plot, "T1")|startsWith(Plot, "T2")|startsWith(Plot, "T3"), "EX_2024", 
  ifelse(startsWith(Plot, "T4")|startsWith(Plot, "T5")|startsWith(Plot, "T6"), "EX_2020", 
         ifelse(endsWith(Plot, "chablis"), "CONTROL_CHABLIS", "CONTROL"))
))

data <- data %>% column_to_rownames("Plot")
```

## PCA

```{r}
pca_plot <- prcomp(data %>% dplyr::select(-type), scale = TRUE)

## individuals
ind <- as.data.frame(get_pca_ind(pca_plot)$coord[,1:2])
colnames(ind) <- c("PC1", "PC2")
ind$type <- data$type

## variables
var <- data.frame(get_pca_var(pca_plot)$coord[, 1:2])
colnames(var) <- c("PC1", "PC2")
var$nom <- rownames(var)

## percentage variance explain by axes
pca_eig <- get_eig(pca_plot)
eig <- pca_eig[1:2, 2]

## colour
niveaux <- levels(ind$type)
cols <- setNames(c("forestgreen", "orange", "firebrick", "royalblue"), niveaux)


## Plot PCA
ggplot(ind, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2)) +
  # confidence elipse
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = type, fill = type),
               geom = "polygon", level = 0.95, alpha = 0.15) +
  # Variables
  geom_segment(data = var,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm")),
               colour = "grey20", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = var, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, label = nom),
            colour = "grey20", vjust = -0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # plot individuals
  geom_point(aes(colour = type, shape = type, size = 3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +
  # labels
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", round(as.numeric(eig[1]), 1), " %)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(as.numeric(eig[2]), 1), " %)"),
       colour = "Traitement", fill = "Traitement", shape = "Traitement") +
  
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Boxplot

We add the data transect and type for each sensor

TOMST

# Part 2 : Germination of new seedlings

```{r}
DATA = read.csv("ARTEMIA_seedling_monitoring_ALLDATA_09_2026.csv", header=T, sep=",", dec=".") # import all the data we have treated

# File with the characteristics of the plot
Plot_char = read.csv("charachteristics_plot.csv", header=T, sep=",", dec=".")

# We will work only on the new seedlings that have appeared between march and september 2026
Natality_analysis = subset(DATA, DATA$Bague >= 2000)
Natality_analysis = DATA_orange %>% count(Placette)
Natality_analysis = Natality_analysis[-c(46,47), ] # delete TZ
Natality_analysis$Logging = Plot_char$type[match(Natality_analysis$Placette,Plot_char$Placette)]

Natality_analysis$n[is.na(Natality_analysis$n)] =0
```

Now we can explore the data with plot

```{r}
hist(Natality_analysis$n,breaks = 15) # it is Poisson law
ggplot(Natality_analysis, aes(x = factor(Logging),y=n)) + geom_boxplot() 
```

## GLM poisson (processus de comptage)

Application condition to the glm poisson

- No surdespersion : I have a calcul to ckeck surdispersion

- Independance of the DATA (here yes, it is 1 value for 1 placette, no répétition)

- Our data follow a poisson distribution

We do the model

```{r}
model_poisson = glm(n~Logging,family="poisson", data=Natality_analysis)
```

We check if the data really **follow a poisson distribution**

```{r}
# To obtain the lambda parameter 
mean(Natality_analysis$n) #  8.673469

# 
set.seed(1234) # allow to simulate count
theoretic_count <-rpois(49,8.673469) # 49 = number of observation and 8.6 is our lambda parameter

# put the theoric counting in a data frame
tc_df <-data.frame(theoretic_count)

# we plot together our data and the simulate data with the poisson law of lamba 8.6
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(Natality_analysis,aes(n))+
  geom_bar(fill="#1E90FF")+
  geom_bar(data=tc_df, aes(theoretic_count,fill="#1E90FF", alpha=0.5))+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position="none")
```

It seems that our data do not follow a poisson law.

We check for surdispersion

```{r}
summary(model_poisson)
model_poisson |> 
  performance::check_overdispersion()
```

We can observe the dispersion ration : residual déviance (252.33) / DDL (41) = 6.846

It is really superior to 0, there is surdispersion (p-value inferior to 0.05)

Therefore, we chose to use a **negative binomiale distribution** (better than quasi-poisson model pour lesquels nous ne savons pas évaluer la correction de la surdispersion).

Package MASS

## GLM negative binomial

```{r}
model_negbin_0 = MASS::glm.nb( n ~ 1, data = Natality_analysis) # nul model AIC: 318.24 and  residual deviance = 55.087

model_negbin_Logged = MASS::glm.nb( n ~ Logging, data = Natality_analysis) # we had the variable logging
summary(model_negbin_Logged)# AIC: 303.99 and Residual deviance: 54.782
```

```{r}
model_negbin_Logged |>
  guideR::observed_vs_theoretical()
model_negbin_Logged |>
  performance::check_predictions(type = "discrete_both")
```

We see that our data follow the negative binomial

```{r}
model_negbin_Logged |> 
  performance::check_overdispersion()
```

No overdispersion

We test if the variable explain significantly the number of seedlings per 10m2

```{r}
anova(model_negbin_Logged) # the type significaly explain the differences of new number of seedlings per plot
```

We can now test per pairs with emmeans

```{r}
emm = emmeans(model_negbin_Logged,"Logging")
summary(emm)
pairs = (pairs(emm))
summary(pairs)
pairs = as.data.frame(pairs) 
```

Now we can represent our data

```{r}

# Transforme the results of emmeans in table
res = as.data.frame(pairs)
res = res %>% filter(p.value < 0.05)
res$group1 = str_split_fixed(res$contrast, " - ", 2)[, 1]
res$group2 = str_split_fixed(res$contrast, " - ", 2)[, 2]

res$label = paste0("\np = ", format.pval(res$p.value, digits = 2))

# For the graphic
maximum = max(Natality_analysis$n, na.rm = TRUE)
pas = max(1, maximum * 0.12)
res$y.position = maximum + pas *
  seq_len(nrow(res))

# Now add to the graphic

ggplot(Natality_analysis, aes(Logging, n, fill = Logging)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_pvalue_manual(res,label = "label",xmin = "group1", xmax = "group2",y.position = "y.position",tip.length = 0.01,inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  labs( title = "Boxplot of the number of new seedlings per 10m2 according to logging", y = "Number of new seedlings/10m2", x = "Logging", fill = "Traitement") +theme_light() +theme( plot.title = element_text(colour = "black",face = "bold"))


```

```{r}
New_character = subset(New_character, New_character$Placette !="TCZ4")
```

```{r}
boxplot(New_character$D_moy_09.26~New_character$Logging) # seems to be bigger for exploited area

boxplot(New_character$N_feuil_09.26~New_character$Logging) # more leaf for 2024
boxplot(New_character$Folmax_09.26~New_character$Logging) # almost only 1 foliole max
```

Now starting the models

### Diameter

```{r}
new_diameter = lm(D_moy_09.26~Logging, data=New_character)
shapiro.test(new_diameter$residuals) # not normal
bptest(new_diameter) # not homocedasticity
dwtest(new_diameter) # independant
plot(new_diameter)

# We did a Krustal-Wallis test
krustal_diameter= kruskal.test(D_moy_09.26 ~ Logging, data  = New_character) # significant difference

# Then test post hoc
wilcox_test(New_character,D_moy_09.26~Logging, paired = F, p.adjust.method = "holm")

# Graphique representation (do not keep for the report)
ggplot(New_character, aes(x = factor(Logging), y = D_moy_09.26,)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill="lightblue", outliers=F) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  labs(title = "Diameter of new seedlings according to the logging condition",x = "Logging condition", y = "Diameter (mm)", subtitle = "Kruskal-Wallis test , p-value = 1.247e-15") + theme(plot.title = element_text(colour = "black",face = "bold"), plot.subtitle=element_text(face="italic"))+
  theme_minimal()

```

Information about non-parametric test :

**Kruskal-Wallis** : non-parametric test (residuals do not need to follow a normal law). But the data need to be ordinal (which is the case with logging variable) and independent.

Here we study the rank (not the mean).

Question of research : Does it exist a difference for the central trend of the 4 different samples study.

H0 : The study variable (diameter or height) is the same between all the groups, there is no difference in the central trend.

H1 : At least one group present systematically higher or lower value than the other groups for the variable study. Therefore, it's distribution varies from the one of the other.

If there is no difference between groups, the mean value of rank will be similar for all the groups.

**Test post-hoc** : Pairwise Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests : allow to compare between group levels with the correction for multiple testing.

### Height

```{r}
new_height = lm(Haut_cm_09.26~Logging, data=New_character)
shapiro.test(new_height$residuals) # not normal
bptest(new_height) # not homocedasticity
dwtest(new_height) # independant
plot(new_height)

# We need to do a non parametric test
kruskal.test(Haut_cm_09.26 ~ Logging, data  = New_character) # significant difference 

# Then post-hoc test

# Test par paires avec détails
wilcox_test(New_character,Haut_cm_09.26~Logging, paired = F, p.adjust.method = "holm")
pairwise.wilcox.test(New_character$Haut_cm_09.26, New_character$Logging, paired = F)

# Graphic 
ggplot(New_character, aes(x = factor(Logging), y = Haut_cm_09.26,)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill="lightblue", outliers=F) + # we do not represent outliers for a better understanding of the graphic
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  labs(title = "Height of new seedlings according to the condition of logging",x = "Logging condition", y = "Height (cm)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Analyse the mortality of the seedlings

First selected the variable and creat variable for seedling densité par placette and pourcentage of herbivorie per seedlings

```{r}
# Prepare the data set 
DATA_mortality = subset(DATA, DATA$Bague<2000) # take only pink

DATA_mortality = select(DATA_mortality,Transect,Placette,Type,Bague,Piquet_ref,Azimut,Dist_m,Etat_09.25,Etat_09.26,Folmax_09.25,Folmax_03.26,N_feuil_09.25,N_herb_09.25,Herb_1_09.25,Herb_2_09.25,Herb_3_09.25,Herb_4_09.25,Herb_5_09.25,N_feuil_03.26,N_herb_03.26,Herb_1_03.26,Herb_2_03.26,Herb_3_03.26,Herb_4_03.26,Herb_5_03.26, Dist_skid_trails,D_moy_09.25,D_moy_03.26) # select the variable

# Take out the control genetic
DATA_mortality = subset(DATA_mortality, DATA_mortality$Type !="CONTROL_GENET")

# Create the variable of density per 10m2 (chose the number of seedlings in 09.2025)
Density_seedlings = DATA_mortality %>% subset(Etat_09.25 =="V") %>%count(Placette)

DATA_mortality$Density= Density_seedlings$n[match(DATA_mortality$Placette, Density_seedlings$Placette)]

# Creat 1 colonne for foliole max 
DATA_mortality$Folmax = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$Folmax_09.25), DATA_mortality$Folmax_03.26, DATA_mortality$Folmax_09.25)

# Create the variable of herbivory when we see the plant for the first time

DATA_mortality$N_feuil = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$N_feuil_09.25), DATA_mortality$N_feuil_03.26, DATA_mortality$N_feuil_09.25)

DATA_mortality$N_herb = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$N_herb_09.25), DATA_mortality$N_herb_03.26, DATA_mortality$N_herb_09.25)

DATA_mortality$Herb_1 = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$Herb_1_09.25), DATA_mortality$Herb_1_03.26, DATA_mortality$Herb_1_09.25)

DATA_mortality$Herb_2 = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$Herb_2_09.25), DATA_mortality$Herb_2_03.26, DATA_mortality$Herb_2_09.25)

DATA_mortality$Herb_3 = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$Herb_3_09.25), DATA_mortality$Herb_3_03.26, DATA_mortality$Herb_3_09.25)

DATA_mortality$Herb_4 = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$Herb_4_09.25), DATA_mortality$Herb_4_03.26, DATA_mortality$Herb_4_09.25)

DATA_mortality$Herb_5 = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$Herb_5_09.25), DATA_mortality$Herb_5_03.26, DATA_mortality$Herb_5_09.25)

# Mean of the herbovie on the leaf eaten
DATA_mortality$Herb_mean = rowMeans(DATA_mortality[,c(31:35)],na.rm=T)

DATA_mortality$Herb_mean[DATA_mortality$Herb_mean=="NaN"]=0
DATA_mortality$Herb_mean =  DATA_mortality$Herb_mean / 10 # to have frequencies

DATA_mortality$Herb_plant = (DATA_mortality$Herb_mean * DATA_mortality$N_herb) / DATA_mortality$N_feuil

# We can select the variables
DATA_mortality_final = select(DATA_mortality,Placette,Type,Bague,Piquet_ref,Azimut,Dist_m,Etat_09.26,Folmax,Density,Herb_plant, Dist_skid_trails) # select the variable

# We add the logged variable
DATA_mortality_final$Logging = Natality_analysis$Logging[match(DATA_mortality_final$Placette, Natality_analysis$Placette)]

# We transform V into 1 en Morte into 0
DATA_mortality_final$Etat = ifelse(DATA_mortality_final$Etat_09.26=="V",1,0)

# Define the number of leaflet max as character
DATA_mortality_final$Folmax = as.character(DATA_mortality_final$Folmax)

# We add the diameter 
DATA_mortality_final$Diameter = ifelse(is.na(DATA_mortality$D_moy_09.25),DATA_mortality$D_moy_03.26, DATA_mortality$D_moy_09.25)

# Select 
DATA_mortality_final = select(DATA_mortality_final,Placette,Type,Bague,Etat,Folmax,Density,Herb_plant,Logging, Diameter)

DATA_mortality_final = na.omit(DATA_mortality_final)

```

Now we can creat our model

```{r}
nul_model_mortality = glmer(Etat ~1 + (1 | Placette), data=DATA_mortality_final,family = binomial(link="logit"))
summary(nul_model_mortality) # 2381.7 et deviance = 2377.7

model1_mortality = glmer(Etat~ Logging + (1 | Placette), data=DATA_mortality_final,family = binomial(link="logit"))
summary(model1_mortality)# 2358.6  et deviance = 2348.6
Anova(model1_mortality) # Logging is significant

model2_mortality = glmer(Etat~ Logging + Density + (1 | Placette), data=DATA_mortality_final,family = binomial(link="logit"))
summary(model2_mortality) # AIC= 2360.6  and deviance = 2348.6
Anova(model2_mortality, type = 2) # density is not significant

model3_mortality = glmer(Etat~ Logging + Herb_plant + (1 | Placette), data=DATA_mortality_final,family = binomial(link="logit"))
summary(model3_mortality) # AIC : 2360.0 and deviance : 2348.0 
Anova(model3_mortality, type = 2) # Herb_plant is significant

model3_mortality_bis = glmer(Etat~ Logging + Diameter + (1 | Placette), data=DATA_mortality_final,family = binomial(link="logit"))
summary(model3_mortality_bis) # AIC : 2277.7 and deviance : 2265.7 
Anova(model3_mortality_bis, type = 2) # Diameter is highly significant

model4_mortality = glmer(Etat~ Logging * Diameter + (1 | Placette), data=DATA_mortality_final,family = binomial(link="logit"))
summary(model4_mortality) # AIC :  2278.9    and deviance : 2260.9
Anova(model4_mortality, type = 2) # The interaction is not significant

model5_mortality = glmer(Etat~ Logging + Herb_plant + Diameter + (1 | Placette), data=DATA_mortality_final,family = binomial(link="logit"))
summary(model5_mortality) # AIC :   2279.7     and deviance :  2265.7 (we can not use the number of leaflet because it is to unbalanced)
Anova(model5_mortality, type = 2)


```

Conclusion : herbivory and density are not significant.

The best model is with diameter and logging, without interaction.

Best model

```{r}
model_mortality = glmer(Etat~ Logging + Diameter + (1 | Placette), data=DATA_mortality_final,family = binomial(link="logit"))
summary(model3_mortality_bis) # AIC : 2277.7 and deviance : 2265.7 
Anova(model3_mortality_bis, type = 2) # Diameter is highly significant
```

We do emmeans test

```{r}
emmeans(model_mortality, pairwise ~  Logging, type = "response",adjust = "tukey", mode="only")
```
